Syllabus guides

The full CSCA syllabus, subject by subject.

Three subjects, four to five topics each, and a fixed set of traps. The guides below break each subject into its components, flag the concepts that come up the most, and link straight to the practice questions that target them.

Start with the playbook

Subject selection, study plan, practice strategy, registration, and submission — written for students new to the CSCA.

The complete student guide

CSCA Exam 2027: subject selection, study plan, practice strategy, and preparation.

The full playbook in one read. A five-step method for picking the right subjects and paper languages, a 12-week and a 30-day plan, the “understand, practise, reflect, repeat” cycle, registration and technical prep, the results-to-university workflow, and a master checklist.

How to use these guides

Each subject guide is structured the same way so you can build a routine around it.

Step 01

Read the syllabus breakdown

Confirm the topics line up with the official CSC syllabus. If a topic looks unfamiliar, that's your first signal — start there.

Step 02

Map your baseline

Take the platform's placement diagnostic. The per-topic weakness map tells you which sections of the guide to start with.

Step 03

Drill by topic, not by subject

Don't try to cover the whole guide in one sitting. One topic per session, ten to fifteen questions, then read every wrong answer.

Step 04

Re-test with a mock

After two to three topic sessions, take the 48-question mock for that subject. The mock report will tell you whether the topic drilling actually stuck.
